title: Distraction Reframing
opening: A useful video idea can wait. A wrong price changes the work now. When the same alert returns, change the setup.

labels.setupChange: What setup change would reduce this repeat interruption?

cases.label: A video idea
cases.summary: A plan-comparison walkthrough could help later, but it does not change the pricing explanation you are writing.

cases.label: A pricing contradiction
cases.summary: The draft says $29 per month; the current example pricing sheet says $19. The correction changes this explanation.

cases.label: The same alert again
cases.summary: A non-urgent project alert interrupts each time you work on the pricing explanation.

example.draftLine: The starter plan costs $29 per month.
example.approvedLine: The starter plan costs $19 per month.
example.setupChange: Pause non-urgent project alerts during drafting; keep urgent contacts available.

practice.result: A private record of your chosen task, captured later idea, current draft correction, or setup change.

feedback.unavailable: Private saving is unavailable. Your work remains on screen.
feedback.missing: Choose a response before saving this note.
feedback.length: Shorten the saved note to 2,000 characters or fewer. Your full text remains here.
feedback.readFailure: The saved note could not be loaded. Your current work remains here.
feedback.conflict: This note changed elsewhere. Your work remains here; save again to keep this version.
feedback.readbackFailure: The save could not be confirmed. Retry to check the same save.
feedback.saveFailure: The save is uncertain. Retry the same save before changing it.
feedback.retryPending: The earlier save is unresolved. Retry the same note before changing it.
feedback.ideaNotConfirmed: The idea is still on screen, but its private save has not been confirmed. Use the private record below to retry or check the result.

source.sourceSpan: When a significant distraction appears, briefly ask whether it supplies something useful to the present question. Capture a useful connection, or save the unrelated question for later. Return to the task. Notice a recurring interruption that requires a change in the arrangement rather than the same repeated decision.
source.attribution: [S01] Supplied Manuscript — 82-page edition. Authorship/adoption of every wording is not independently established.
source.effectLimit: This practice teaches a classification and next action. It makes no claim that the interaction itself improves attention or performance.

teaching.materialCorrection: The example pricing sheet says $19 per month; update the line in the explanation before continuing.
teaching.recurringPattern: When the same alert keeps interrupting, change one relevant part of the setup instead of making the same decision again.
